title: Slack Alternatives for Team Messaging and Collaboration
description: Compare alternatives to Slack across workplace chat, community messaging, meetings, and unified communications. This is not a free-only shortlist; verify current free-tier eligibility, plan limits, retention, and export options directly with each vendor.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Teams
alternatives.description: A workplace collaboration option combining messaging and meetings with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. Evaluate guest access, administration, file collaboration, retention, and licensing for the exact organization plan.

alternatives.name: Discord
alternatives.description: A community-oriented platform with text channels, voice, and video. It may fit open communities or developer groups better than regulated internal communications; test governance, retention, access controls, and workplace policy fit.

alternatives.name: Zoom
alternatives.description: A meetings-first platform with related collaboration and chat capabilities. Compare it when external meetings are central, and test whether its team messaging, search, and channel workflows meet the needs currently handled in Slack.

alternatives.name: RingCentral
alternatives.description: A unified communications option combining business phone, meetings, and team messaging. Evaluate it when calling and messaging need to share administration; confirm the exact messaging features and plan entitlements.

alternatives.name: Dialpad
alternatives.description: A business communications platform centered on phone workflows and call-related tools, with messaging capabilities. It is most relevant when sales or support calling is part of the decision; verify that its chat experience meets your team's Slack replacement needs.

faqs.question: What should I compare when replacing Slack?
faqs.answer: Test channel structure, search, threads, notifications, file sharing, guest access, retention, administration, integrations, mobile use, and exports. Use the same team workflow and representative message history across candidates.

faqs.question: Are these all free Slack alternatives?
faqs.answer: No. This shortlist includes different workplace messaging and unified-communications products. Free plans, trials, usage limits, and commercial entitlements change; verify current vendor terms before budgeting.

faqs.question: Which option is closest to Slack for workplace chat?
faqs.answer: That depends on your team's needs and ecosystem. Microsoft Teams is relevant for organizations using Microsoft 365; Discord is more community-oriented; Zoom, RingCentral, and Dialpad may suit teams that prioritize meetings or calling. Pilot the actual channel and governance workflow rather than assuming feature parity.

faqs.question: Are the ratings on this page verified?
faqs.answer: No. The linked review records contain stored editorial scores that are not marked verified. They are not independent customer-rating averages or benchmark results, so use the criteria and a hands-on pilot rather than treating the numbers as proof.

faqs.question: Can I migrate Slack messages and files?
faqs.answer: Migration depends on the source export, destination import capabilities, plan permissions, and retention policies. Test a small representative export first, verify what cannot be transferred, and preserve required records and access controls.

faqs.question: How do I compare total cost?
faqs.answer: Include user and guest licensing, meeting or calling requirements, storage, retention, compliance controls, integrations, administration, onboarding, and renewal terms. Compare the exact plan and expected user count using current vendor documentation.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Slack is a channel-based team messaging workspace with search and integrations. Alternatives vary substantially: some focus on workplace collaboration, some on public or private communities, and others combine messaging with phone or meeting services. The options here are not a free-only ranking or a claim of equivalent functionality. Stored ratings are unverified; choose based on the communication workflow, governance, and integrations your team actually needs.

sections.title: How to evaluate the shortlist
sections.body: Run a pilot with the same team and a realistic set of channels, threads, files, external guests, and notifications. Test search, message retention, admin controls, mobile use, integration behavior, and export or migration paths. Confirm which features are included in the exact plan, and record any workflow that needs a manual workaround.

selectionCriteria: Messaging fit: compare channels, threads, search, notifications, file sharing, and mobile workflows.
Governance: verify guest controls, retention, eDiscovery or audit needs, access policies, and offboarding.
Ecosystem: test the integrations and identity setup your team already uses.
Communication scope: decide whether chat alone or chat plus meetings and phone is required.
Total cost and portability: include seats, add-ons, migration, administration, renewal, and data export.
